_meta.note: Candidates derived from literature gaps, not from the OS-Tutor-RAG architecture. Prior-art depth is LIMITED (see docs/LITERATURE_SEARCH_LOG.md): every 'closest_prior_art' is what the searches surfaced, not a proof of absence. Statuses are ordinal labels, not acceptance predictions. Evidence tags: FULL/PARTIAL/ABSTRACT/SNIPPET denote how deeply the cited paper was read.
_meta.origin_labels: LITERATURE-DERIVED = would be a good problem had OS-Tutor-RAG never been built; PROJECT-ANCHORED = only interesting because of the repo.

candidates.title: A validated operating-systems misconception inventory (item bank with psychometrics)
candidates.gap: MISSING DATASET: the only OS inventory found (Webb and Taylor 2014, 10 items) states it is not yet validated; other OS misconception work is small qualitative studies (9 and 78 students).
candidates.evidence: osci2014 (FULL), upm2017 (PARTIAL), koli2013 (ABSTRACT). Validated inventories exist for adjacent topics (dynamic programming, 172 students; cybersecurity, 354 students; SNIPPET), so the method is established.
candidates.research_question: Can a psychometrically validated OS concept inventory (reliability, discrimination, distractor analysis) covering processes, memory and concurrency be built, and what misconceptions dominate?
candidates.hypothesis: A 25-40 item bank reaches acceptable reliability and identifies a small set of dominant distractor-driven misconceptions per topic, replicating across cohorts.
candidates.method: Item development from course material and known misconceptions; expert review; administration to multiple cohorts; classical test theory and IRT; distractor analysis.
candidates.data: Real student responses from at least 2 cohorts (needs a few hundred responses). Availability UNKNOWN.
candidates.baselines: Webb and Taylor 2014 items; instructor exam items.
candidates.primary_metric: Cronbach alpha / IRT reliability, item discrimination, distractor selection rates.
candidates.closest_prior_art: osci2014; Cybersecurity CI and Dynamic Programming CI psychometrics (SNIPPET); Practical Details of Building a CS Concept Inventory (title only).
candidates.difference: OS scope with validated psychometrics; ties to later LLM evaluation (C02, C06).
candidates.novelty_risk: Medium: an OS inventory follow-up may exist but was not found (search thin).
candidates.feasibility: Needs cohort access and ethics approval; slow; the resource itself is the contribution.
candidates.kill_test: If fewer than about 150 usable responses can be obtained, or reliability stays below about 0.6 after two revisions, abandon.

candidates.title: Correctness audit of LLM explanations of OS mechanisms, stratified by static vs state-dependent claims
candidates.gap: MISSING EVALUATION: no study found evaluating LLM correctness on OS-concept explanations; OS LLM work is a TA system with no evaluation (SortingHat) and 6-question grading (Grade Like a Human).
candidates.evidence: sortinghat2025 (FULL), gradelike2024 (PARTIAL); OS-specific searches found nothing else (thin search).
candidates.research_question: Where do LLM explanations of OS mechanisms go wrong, and are errors concentrated in state-dependent explanations (traces, timing, ordering)?
candidates.hypothesis: Claim-level error rates are higher for dynamic, state-dependent claims than for definitional claims, for the same models.
candidates.method: Collect explanations from several LLMs on human-authored questions; decompose into claims; two experts label each claim; analyze by claim type and model.
candidates.data: Human-authored OS questions (from course exams/textbook), expert labels.
candidates.primary_metric: Claim-level error rate by claim type with confidence intervals; inter-rater kappa.
candidates.closest_prior_art: Demystify (2512.00215), CES (2510.15079): code-execution errors, Python only.
candidates.difference: OS mechanisms and prose explanations with expert claim-level labels.
candidates.feasibility: Feasible with two annotators; cost is annotation time.
candidates.repo_helps: Real course corpus and the RAG pipeline as one system under test.
candidates.kill_test: If overall claim error rate on strong models is below about 5% (little to study), or kappa below 0.6 after guideline revision, abandon.

candidates.title: What do executable checks detect that LLM judges and NLI miss? Claim-level verification of OS explanations
candidates.gap: MISSING EVALUATION: MechSim and FAX check claims with simulators or tools but report LLM-judge scores or faithfulness, not claim-level precision/recall against independent ground truth; FAX warns verification is only local.
candidates.research_question: On OS explanations with known injected and natural errors, do simulator-execution checks achieve higher claim-level recall and lower false-accept than cross-family LLM judges, NLI and RAGAS-style metrics?
candidates.hypothesis: Execution checks catch state-dependent errors that judges and entailment miss, but cover only a fraction of claims.
candidates.method: Expert-labelled claim set (from C02) plus injected errors of controlled types; run four verifier families; report per-error-type recall and false-accept with paired tests.
candidates.data: C02 claim set; deterministic simulators (existing repo code, to be rewritten to accept structured claims).
candidates.baselines: Cross-family LLM judge, NLI, RAGAS faithfulness, majority of judges.
candidates.primary_metric: Recall and false-accept rate per error type; coverage (fraction of claims checkable).
candidates.difference: Controlled injected-error comparison in a discrete-state domain with independent expert labels; reports coverage, which prior work leaves out.
candidates.novelty_risk: HIGH for any 'method' claim (idea exists); moderate for the evaluation framing.
candidates.feasibility: Moderate: needs claim-to-contract translation and simulator coverage.
candidates.repo_helps: Simulators (src/verification) and pipeline; contracts need rewrite.
candidates.kill_test: If a cross-family LLM judge matches the simulator's recall within the confidence interval on state-dependent errors, or claim coverage is below about 30%, abandon the executable-verification thrust.

candidates.title: Claim-coverage audit: what fraction of real tutor-answer claims is executable-checkable?
candidates.gap: MISSING EVALUATION: FAX states verification coverage is limited by available tools; coverage is rarely reported.
candidates.research_question: What proportion of claims in LLM answers to real OS questions can a simulator or program check?
candidates.hypothesis: Coverage is low for conceptual answers and high only for trace/numeric questions.
candidates.method: Annotate claims from C02 answers as checkable/not checkable; estimate coverage by question type.
candidates.primary_metric: Coverage with confidence interval by question type.
candidates.difference: First step; makes the verification claim honest.
candidates.novelty_risk: Low but small on its own.
candidates.kill_test: Coverage under about 30% overall means executable verification is not viable as a general tutor safeguard.

candidates.title: Does a correct OS trace imply a correct causal explanation? Forward simulation vs causal attribution on scheduler/paging traces
candidates.gap: UNTESTED CAUSAL CLAIM: TempoBench shows 75-96% forward simulation vs 21-33% minimal causal attribution on synthetic Mealy machines; not tested on OS mechanisms or prose explanations.
candidates.research_question: For scheduler and paging scenarios, how often are LLM step-by-step traces correct while their stated causes are wrong?
candidates.hypothesis: Trace correctness overstates causal correctness by a large margin.
candidates.method: Textbook-style problems with simulator-derived ground truth; ask for trace and cause; score both.
candidates.data: Human-authored problem variants (not templates); simulator ground truth.
candidates.primary_metric: Trace accuracy minus cause accuracy, paired.
candidates.novelty_risk: Medium-high (PetriBench and TempoBench are close in spirit).
candidates.kill_test: If gap between trace and cause accuracy is within noise, abandon.

candidates.title: Validity of automated correctness scoring for OS tutor answers: teacher-labelled agreement of same- vs cross-family judges
candidates.gap: INVALID/WEAK EVALUATION ASSUMPTION: judge agreement is shown for chat preference (MT-Bench) but no study of judge validity on tutoring or OS answers was found; self-preference evidence is contested.
candidates.evidence: mtbench2023, narcissist2026, selfprefverif2026, factmetrics2024, mrbench2025 (PARTIAL/FULL). Counter-evidence: RAGAS reports high agreement on WikiEval and an educational Q&A set (SNIPPET).
candidates.research_question: How well do judges and RAGAS-style metrics agree with teacher claim-level labels on OS answers, and does same-family judging inflate scores?
candidates.hypothesis: Agreement is lower for state-dependent errors, and refusal inflates faithfulness scores.
candidates.method: Score the same C02 answers with same-family and cross-family judges and metrics; compare with teacher labels; paired analysis with clustered SEs.
candidates.primary_metric: Agreement (kappa/AUROC) with teacher labels by error type; abstention effect.
candidates.closest_prior_art: MT-Bench, MRBench, RAGAS validation (SNIPPET), Sufficient Context.
candidates.difference: OS/education domain with expert claim-level labels and explicit refusal analysis.
candidates.novelty_risk: Medium (generic judge-validity work is abundant; domain-specific piece is the gap).
candidates.repo_helps: Real measurements on faithfulness and noise (small n).
candidates.kill_test: If cross-family judge agreement with teachers is as high as human-human agreement across error types, the blind spot is not there; abandon.

candidates.title: Faithfulness-abstention confound in RAG metrics on course corpora
candidates.gap: WEAKLY EVIDENCED: project finding A1 (faithfulness rewards refusal), n = 26; Sufficient Context motivates but does not test metrics.
candidates.research_question: How much of a faithfulness score is attributable to abstention rather than correctness?
candidates.hypothesis: Forced abstention raises faithfulness at zero correctness.
candidates.method: Score identical answers under forced-abstain vs forced-answer policies, stratified by context sufficiency.
candidates.data: Course corpus with expanded question set.
candidates.kill_test: If refusal-aware metrics already remove the effect, fold into C06 as a sub-analysis.

candidates.title: Noise-floor and power audit of published RAG / LLM-tutor evaluations
candidates.gap: MISSING EVALUATION (adoption): methods exist (Miller, Card); RAG/tutor-specific audit not found, but the search for run-to-run noise in RAG failed.
candidates.research_question: How many published RAG/tutor comparisons have differences within their own noise?
candidates.hypothesis: A majority report gains below a plausible noise floor.
candidates.method: Systematic audit plus re-estimation of power and intervals.
candidates.primary_metric: Share of comparisons that are underpowered.
candidates.novelty_risk: Medium: audit-style; might duplicate Bean et al. in scope.
candidates.kill_test: If Bean et al. or a RAG-specific audit already reports this, abandon.

candidates.title: Chunker x query-expansion x reranker x generator factorial at fixed context budget on a real OS corpus
candidates.gap: UNTESTED INTERACTION: chunking, expansion and reranking effects are studied one at a time; effect signs flip with retriever strength.
candidates.evidence: expfail2024, chunkcliff2026, longctxrag2024, semchunk2024 (PARTIAL); project A16 shows reranking helps single-query and hurts multi-query.
candidates.research_question: Which interactions among chunker, expansion, reranker and generator are real once run-to-run noise is controlled?
candidates.hypothesis: Reranking and multi-query interact negatively; chunker effects vanish with a strong reranker.
candidates.method: Full factorial with repeated runs, paired significance, fixed token budget.
candidates.data: 37-file OS corpus plus human-authored, independently reviewed question set (larger than 26).
candidates.primary_metric: Answer correctness and context hit, paired with clustered SEs.
candidates.repo_helps: Pipeline and harness are the instrument.
candidates.kill_test: If interactions are within the measured noise floor, the contribution reduces to a null result.

candidates.title: Cross-concept questions: vector vs GraphRAG vs hybrid at matched cost on OS material
candidates.gap: Partly addressed; cross-concept questions where GraphRAG may help are explicitly untested (2509.16780).
candidates.research_question: Does GraphRAG help on cross-concept OS questions once cost and context size are matched?
candidates.hypothesis: GraphRAG gains disappear at matched context.
candidates.method: Matched-compute comparison.
candidates.kill_test: Abandon if any of the four existing studies already ran matched-cost comparisons.

candidates.title: Misconception-conditioned retrieval with validated OS misconceptions
candidates.gap: The only controlled test found is null (wrong-answer conditioning gave no clear benefit on SciQ, whose distractors are not validated misconceptions).
candidates.research_question: With validated misconceptions, does misconception-conditioned retrieval improve support-passage retrieval?
candidates.hypothesis: Benefit appears only when misconceptions are validated and specific.
candidates.method: Requires C01 items.
candidates.difference: Validated OS misconceptions and the shuffled control.
candidates.kill_test: Null result with narrow CI means abandon.

candidates.title: Fidelity of LLM-simulated students on OS misconceptions vs real distractor distributions
candidates.gap: Simulated-student validity is contested (Benedetto r = 0.13; competence paradox).
candidates.evidence: benedetto2024 (FULL), yuan2026student (PARTIAL); new leads 2605.12748 and 2603.15547 (SNIPPET, unread).
candidates.research_question: Do simulated students reproduce real OS distractor choice distributions?
candidates.hypothesis: Fidelity is low without persona grounding.
candidates.method: Compare simulated vs real response distributions on C01 items.
candidates.kill_test: Abandon if 2605.12748/2603.15547 already cover it.

candidates.title: Do tutor-quality benchmark scores predict learning gains?
candidates.gap: HUMAN/EDUCATIONAL OUTCOME GAP: no paper links MRBench/MathTutorBench scores to measured learning.
candidates.research_question: Does benchmark ranking of tutors predict post-test gains?
candidates.hypothesis: Correlation is weak.
candidates.method: Multi-tutor RCT.
candidates.feasibility: Very hard (needs many students and tutors).
candidates.kill_test: Cannot recruit enough participants for adequate power: abandon.

candidates.title: Guardrail components and delayed retention for an OS-course LLM tutor (factorial RCT)
candidates.gap: Which guardrail component prevents dependency is unresolved; systems courses unstudied.
candidates.evidence: bastani2025 (ABSTRACT), dissociation2026 (ABSTRACT), guardrails2026 (PARTIAL); new leads 2606.01375 (delayed retention), 2608.12292 (SNIPPET).
candidates.research_question: Which tutor guardrails preserve learning after AI removal in an OS course?
candidates.hypothesis: Answer withholding drives retention.
candidates.method: Factorial RCT with a two-week delayed no-help test.
candidates.kill_test: Abandon if cohort power is below about 0.8 for a 0.3 SD effect.

candidates.title: Perceived helpfulness vs learning for an OS tutor
candidates.gap: Perception and learning dissociate (dissociation RCT, ai2503).
candidates.research_question: Does perceived helpfulness predict OS learning gains?
candidates.hypothesis: No.
candidates.method: Pre/post plus survey.
candidates.kill_test: Already answered in adjacent domains: abandon.

candidates.title: Simulator-grounded generation vs post-hoc verification for OS explanations
candidates.gap: Simulator output can be injected before generation (Mind's Eye) or used to audit after (MechSim); no OS comparison.
candidates.research_question: Is grounding at generation time better than post-hoc checking for correctness and coverage?
candidates.hypothesis: Post-hoc catches more but costs more.
candidates.method: Two pipelines compared on C02 items.
candidates.kill_test: No gap between the two: abandon.

candidates.title: Robustness of course-grounded tutors to plausible but wrong passages
candidates.gap: SECURITY/ROBUSTNESS GAP for educational RAG; adjacent evidence (PoisonedRAG, RGB, GSM-IC).
candidates.research_question: How often do tutors adopt wrong textbook passages?
candidates.hypothesis: Adoption is high when passages are fluent.
candidates.method: Inject counterfactual passages.
candidates.kill_test: Adoption near zero: abandon.

candidates.title: Multi-version and multi-format lecture duplicates in tutor retrieval
candidates.gap: Local data-quality issue; deduplication work exists (byte-exact dedup in RAG, 2605.09611, SNIPPET).
candidates.evidence: corpus has PDF+PPTX pairs and two versions of several lectures.
candidates.research_question: Does version duplication bias retrieval?
candidates.hypothesis: Yes, mildly.
candidates.method: Ablate duplicates.
candidates.kill_test: Treat as a control, not a paper.

candidates.title: Abstention thresholds for course-grounded tutors using context sufficiency
candidates.gap: Sufficient context studied on QA, not tutors.
candidates.research_question: Can a sufficiency signal reduce wrong answers in tutoring without excess refusals?
candidates.hypothesis: Yes at some cost.
candidates.method: Autorater plus selective generation.
candidates.kill_test: No coverage/accuracy gain: abandon.

candidates.title: IRT-based difficulty calibration of LLM-authored OS questions vs expert ratings
candidates.gap: IRT usefulness for LLM benchmarks is contested (Madaan); transfer to templated or LLM-authored items untested.
candidates.research_question: Do LLM-based IRT difficulties match expert or student difficulty for OS items?
candidates.hypothesis: Weak agreement.
candidates.method: Fit IRT; compare.
candidates.kill_test: Correlation above about 0.8 means solved.

candidates.title: LLM-authored OS distractors vs observed student answer distributions
candidates.gap: LLM distractors are mathematically valid but miss real misconceptions (SNIPPET); OS untested.
candidates.research_question: Do LLM distractors match real OS distractor selection?
candidates.hypothesis: Poorly.
candidates.method: Compare with C01 data.
candidates.kill_test: Abandon if the domain difference adds nothing.

candidates.title: OS-state reasoning benchmark with executable ground truth and human-authored problems
candidates.gap: Code-execution benchmarks are Python-centric; concurrency and memory management are named limitations (Demystify); OS-state reasoning untested.
candidates.research_question: How accurately do LLMs predict scheduler, paging and lock state over time on human-authored problems?
candidates.hypothesis: Accuracy drops with state length and concurrency.
candidates.method: Textbook and exam-derived problems with simulator ground truth; error taxonomy.
candidates.difference: OS mechanisms; human-authored variants to avoid template-benchmark criticism.
candidates.kill_test: If frontier models exceed about 95% accuracy, little to study.

candidates.title: Length and position bias when LLM judges score tutor answers
candidates.gap: Length bias has a regression fix (AlpacaEval LC), tested on one benchmark.
candidates.research_question: Do tutor judges reward verbosity?
candidates.hypothesis: Yes.
candidates.method: Controlled length perturbations.
candidates.kill_test: Fold into C06.
